user.title: Connect to WealthyExile
user.description: Log in at wealthyexile.com/stash, open your browser's DevTools (Network tab), pick a request to `stash?primary=true`, and look at its `cookie` header. You'll see two cookies separated by `; ` — e.g. `code_verifier=d31a6d0f-...` and `session-Allflame-1=eyJhbGci...`. Enter both separately below: the name (the word before `=`) on the left, the value (everything after) on the right. Important: the second cookie's name changes with every new PoE league (e.g. `session-Allflame-1` eventually becomes `session-<NewLeague>-1`) — always enter the current name, not an old one.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach WealthyExile. Check your internet connection and try again.
error.parse_failed: Could not read WealthyExile's response — either the cookie is invalid/expired, or WealthyExile updated their site (next-action hash out of date, see const.py).

stash_parse_failed.title: WealthyExile response could not be read, repeatedly
stash_parse_failed.description: A single failure is normal (e.g. if you synced in a browser at the same moment) and self-heals on the next poll — this message only appears after several consecutive failures. Most likely causes: your stored cookie has expired (set up the integration again with a fresh cookie), or WealthyExile updated their site and the hardcoded `next-action` hash is out of date. In the latter case: open your browser's DevTools on wealthyexile.com/stash, look at a `stash?primary=true` request, and update the `next-action` and `x-deployment-id` headers in `const.py`, then restart Home Assistant.
